prologue.speaker: muse
prologue.text: Sing, goddess, of rage. That is how Homer begins the Iliad.

prologue.speaker: muse
prologue.text: Today I sing of a different contest. Its weapons are memory and truth.

prologue.speaker: muse
prologue.text: This duel is not a scene from the poem, but every answer comes from Homer's text.

prologue.speaker: muse
prologue.text: Answer truly and your blow lands. Answer wrongly and your enemy strikes. Three true answers in a row, and you enter your aristeia: a hero's moment of glory.

greek.label: Fight as Achilles
greek.blurb: Greek · swift-footed leader of the Myrmidons

intro.speaker: achilles
intro.text: I have sat beside my ships long enough. Bring me Troy's champions.

victory.speaker: muse
victory.text: Three champions have fallen before Achilles.

victory.speaker: muse
victory.text: In the poem, his rage ends not in triumph but in pity, when he weeps with Priam over Hector's body.

victory.speaker: achilles
victory.text: The glory is mine. But Patroclus is still gone.

trojan.label: Fight as Hector
trojan.blurb: Trojan · tamer of horses, defender of Troy

intro.speaker: hector
intro.text: For Troy, for my father, and for my son. Let them come.

victory.speaker: muse
victory.text: Hector has turned back the Greeks, something the poem never grants him.

victory.speaker: muse
victory.text: In Homer he falls at the Scaean Gate, and the poem ends with his funeral.

victory.speaker: hector
victory.text: Troy stands. Tonight I will hold my son again.

intro.speaker: paris
intro.text: So the great Achilles finally leaves his tent. I am Paris, who brought Helen to Troy.

intro.speaker: paris
intro.text: My arrows strike from far away. Let us see whether your answers do.

paris.defeat: Aphrodite saved me once from Menelaus. Today no goddess comes.
paris.win: Even swift feet cannot outrun an arrow.

intro.speaker: ares
intro.text: I am Ares, and war is my whole nature.

intro.speaker: ares
intro.text: Diomedes wounded me once, with Athena guiding his spear. You have no goddess beside you.

ares.defeat: Wounded again! I will run to my father Zeus, as I did before.
ares.win: Mortals bleed, and the war goes on.

intro.speaker: hector
intro.text: Three times you chased me around these walls. I will not run again.

intro.speaker: hector
intro.text: Let us agree: whoever wins gives the other's body back to his people.

intro.speaker: achilles
intro.text: There are no bargains between us. Answer, and fight.

hector.defeat: Remember my words. Paris and Apollo will bring you down at these same gates.

intro.speaker: menelaus
intro.text: Your brother took my wife from my house in Sparta.

intro.speaker: menelaus
intro.text: He hid behind a goddess's mist. Will you hide too, Hector?

menelaus.defeat: I yield the field. But the Greeks will not sail home without her.
menelaus.win: Sparta's honour is restored, for today.

intro.speaker: ajax
intro.text: We fought once until night fell, and parted with gifts.

intro.speaker: ajax
intro.text: When you brought fire to these ships, I held them. I will hold them again.

ajax.defeat: I stood like a tower. But even towers fall.
ajax.win: The ships are safe. Go back to your walls, Hector.

intro.speaker: achilles
intro.text: You killed Patroclus. Now you face me.

intro.speaker: hector
intro.text: Then let us agree: whoever wins gives the other's body back to his people.

intro.speaker: achilles
intro.text: There are no bargains between us. Answer, and fight.

achilles.defeat: My mother said my life would be short. Shorter than I thought.

defeat.speaker: muse
defeat.text: Even the greatest heroes of the Iliad fall. But memory can be trained. Try again.
